messages.author: c4e67f9d1aa89ddc
messages.subject: First and last 24h not analysed
parts:
Hi Vincent hi all,

Here's a problem that I hadn't encountered until now:

I use 14 days recordings with a start set at 00:00. (When looking at .csv recording actually start at  ~00:00 (i.e. 00:01:00:500) (because of the potential small difference between device time and local pc time I guess)

Then I use the following for part.1/part.2:

dayborder=0,
strategy=1,
hrs.del.start=0,
hrs.del.end=0,
maxdur=14,
includedaycrit=15,
qwindow=c(0,24),
[...]
do.report=c(2)

For all my files, first and last days are NA in daysummary.

Calendar_date is 00:15:00  for day 1 and day 14 and 00:14:55 for all other days.

For measurement day 1 and 14, N.valid.hours is 0.24 (i.e. 14.4 min) explaining why data are not computed for these days.

Any idea what may cause this issue and what would solve it?

R 3.3.3
GGIR 1.4


Thanks,

Damien

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] First and last 24h not analysed
parts:
Hi Damien,
Here are my thoughts:
- Is variable N hours substantially different from N.valid.hours?
- You may want to change argument maxdur to 14.5, such that the analyses also include a bit more than 14 days of data.
- Next, can you have a look at the milestone data (RData) from one of your problematic files and inspect the dimensions of the M$metashort dataframe via command: dim(M$metashort). Do these dimensions matches the 14 days of data you expect?
- Can you also plot the values of the M$metashort$ENMO object to see how the movement pattern varies acros days of measurement?
Best wishes
Vincent

parts:
Hi Vincent,

 

Thank you for your answer.

 

I had tried to change maxdur to 14.5 without success. However, I did it again with overwrite set to TRUE and this solved the problem.

 

The output is efficiently changed when I reduce maxdur (for instance to 7).

 

My understanding is that maxdur is an arguments from g.impute that generate the metashort milestone data so that it can be shorten post hoc but not extended. Is that correct ?

 

Best,

 

Damien

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] First and last 24h not analysed
parts:
Hi Damien,
That is correct. If you want to change these decisions you will need to re-run part2 (which includes g.impute) with overwrite set to TRUE.
I included the maxdur option for studies where the researcher manually needs to turn off the accelerometer after a week of measurement and occasionally forgets to do this by which they have an extra couple of days without movement.
Vincent
